title: Database Object Management & System Catalogs
description: Query pg_class, pg_attribute, and information_schema to inspect schemas, table sizes, and column definitions.

data.text: PostgreSQL stores all database metadata in internal system catalog tables inside the `pg_catalog` schema. Querying catalogs like `pg_class`, `pg_attribute`, and `pg_tables` lets you inspect disk usage, dead tuples, and table structures programmatically.

data.title: Finding the Largest Tables in the Database
data.content: Inspects total table size including indexes.
data.code:
SELECT 
    relname AS table_name,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) AS total_size,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(c.oid)) AS heap_size,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) - pg_relation_size(c.oid)) AS index_size
FROM pg_class c
JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
WHERE n.nspname = 'public' 
  AND c.relkind = 'r'
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) DESC
LIMIT 10;

data.text: PostgreSQL keeps every definition in the `pg_catalog` schema. The SQL-standard `information_schema` is a portable view layer on top of it. Interviewers like the distinction: `information_schema` is portable but slower and incomplete, while `pg_catalog` is PostgreSQL-specific and exposes everything.
The Queries You Will Actually Reuse

data.title: Table Sizes: Heap, Indexes, TOAST, Total
data.content: This is the query that answers "where did all my disk go?".
data.code:
SELECT n.nspname AS schema,
       c.relname AS table_name,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(c.oid))                          AS heap,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size(c.oid))                           AS indexes,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid))                    AS total
FROM pg_class c
JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
WHERE c.relkind = 'r'
  AND n.nspname = 'public'
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) DESC
LIMIT 10;

data.title: Introspect Columns and Constraints
data.content: Replaces guessing at a schema you did not write.
data.code:
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders'
ORDER BY ordinal_position;

-- Constraints with their definitions, straight from the catalog
SELECT con.conname,
       con.contype,                 -- p=PK, f=FK, u=unique, c=check, x=exclusion
       pg_get_constraintdef(con.oid) AS definition
FROM pg_constraint con
JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = con.conrelid
WHERE c.relname = 'orders';

-- Every index on a table, including expression and partial indexes
SELECT indexname, indexdef FROM pg_indexes
WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'orders';

data.title: Live Table Activity
data.content: The starting point for any bloat or vacuum investigation.
data.code:
SELECT relname,
       seq_scan, idx_scan,
       n_live_tup, n_dead_tup,
       round(100.0 * n_dead_tup / GREATEST(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 1), 1) AS dead_pct,
       last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC
LIMIT 10;

data.title: Why This Matters
data.text: Almost every "the database is slow" investigation starts with catalog queries: which table is biggest, which index is unused (`idx_scan = 0`), and how much dead tuple bloat exists. Being fluent here is a strong senior-engineer signal.

data.title: Build a Schema Report
data.description: Write one query that lists each table with its size, row estimate, index count, and dead-tuple percentage.
steps: Order by total size descending and run it against a database with real data.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable health report you could paste into a runbook.

items.question: Should I query `information_schema` or `pg_catalog`?
items.answer: Use `information_schema` for portable, simple questions; use `pg_catalog` when you need PostgreSQL-specific detail such as index definitions, dead tuple counts, or physical sizes.

items.question: How do I find unused indexes?
items.answer: `SELECT relname, indexrelname, idx_scan FROM pg_stat_statements`-adjacent views — specifically `pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE idx_scan = 0`. Drop them only after confirming the statistics window covers a full business cycle (call `pg_stat_reset()` and re-measure).

items.question: Why is a table bigger than the sum of its rows?
items.answer: Dead tuples from MVCC, page padding, TOAST data, and indexes. Use `pgstattuple` for a precise live/dead breakdown.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: All schema metadata lives in `pg_catalog`; `information_schema` is a portable view over it.
`pg_total_relation_size` = heap + indexes + TOAST; always look at all three when sizing a table.
`pg_get_constraintdef` and `pg_get_indexdef` give you back the exact DDL to recreate an object.
`pg_stat_user_tables` exposes scans, live/dead tuples, and last vacuum — the entry point for tuning.
data.takeaway: Being able to introspect a foreign schema with catalog queries is one of the most practical skills in this module.
